subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these would you expect in a highly developed country?
options: High birth rate and low life expectancy
High death rate and low GNI
High life expectancy and high literacy rate
Low literacy and low life expectancy
questions.explain: More developed countries typically have high life expectancy and literacy rates alongside high incomes.

questions.q: In Stage 2 of the Demographic Transition Model, population grows rapidly because:
options: Birth rate falls sharply
Birth rate stays high while death rate falls
Death rate rises above birth rate
Both rates are high and stable
questions.explain: In Stage 2 death rates drop due to better healthcare and food while birth rates remain high, causing rapid growth.

questions.q: Which is an example of a 'pull' factor for migration?
options: Better job opportunities in the destination
Drought at home
Religious persecution at home
War in the home country
questions.explain: Pull factors attract people to a new place; better jobs in the destination is a classic pull factor.

options: There are too few people to use resources fully
Birth and death rates are equal
The population exceeds the resources available to support it
A country has lots of empty land
questions.explain: Overpopulation is when the number of people exceeds the resources and technology available to maintain a good standard of living.

questions.q: In Stage 4 of the Demographic Transition Model, population is typically:
options: Growing very rapidly
Falling steeply
Both rates very high
High and stable with low birth and death rates
questions.explain: In Stage 4 both birth and death rates are low, so the population is high and roughly stable.

questions.q: A dispersed settlement pattern is one where:
options: Buildings are tightly clustered together
All houses are in one block
Buildings are spread out and isolated
Buildings follow a road in a line
questions.explain: In a dispersed pattern, settlements are scattered and isolated, often in remote or upland farming areas.

questions.q: A negative impact of migration on the SOURCE (origin) country is often:
options: A rising birth rate
An increase in its workforce
More money spent locally by migrants
A loss of working-age people and skills ('brain drain')
questions.explain: When working-age and skilled people emigrate, the source country can suffer a 'brain drain' and labour shortages.

questions.q: Natural increase in a population occurs when:
options: The population stays the same
Migration into a country rises
Death rate is higher than birth rate
Birth rate is higher than death rate
questions.explain: Natural increase is when births exceed deaths, causing the population to grow before migration is considered.

questions.q: A benefit of immigration for a HOST country is often:
options: A reduced workforce
Lower economic output
Falling cultural diversity
Filling labour shortages and adding skills
questions.explain: Immigrants can fill gaps in the labour market and bring skills, boosting the host country's economy.

questions.q: On a settlement hierarchy, which has the highest order and largest range of services?
options: A village
A town
A city / conurbation
A hamlet
questions.explain: Cities and conurbations sit at the top of the settlement hierarchy with the largest populations and widest range of services.

questions.q: How can fairer trade help reduce the development gap more than aid?
options: It removes all jobs from poorer countries
It only provides short-term emergency relief
It builds long-term, self-sustaining income for producers
It makes countries permanently dependent on donors
questions.explain: Trade builds lasting income and economic independence, whereas some aid can create dependency.

questions.q: Which factor encourages a high population density?
options: Extreme desert conditions
Dense tropical rainforest with poor soils
Steep mountainous relief
A flat, fertile area with a temperate climate
questions.explain: Flat fertile land with a moderate climate supports farming and settlement, leading to higher population densities.
